title: Smooth compact scalar kernels regularize locally integrable Euclidean functions
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $m\geq1$ and $r\geq0$ be integers. Let $u:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R^r$ be Lebesgue measurable and locally integrable, meaning that $\int_C\|u(y)\|\,dy<\infty$ for every compact $C\subset\mathbf R^m$. Let $h:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R$ be smooth (infinitely real differentiable), and suppose the closure of $\{x:h(x)\ne0\}$ is compact. Then the vector integral $$T_hu(x)=\int_{\mathbf R^m}h(x-y)u(y)\,dy$$ is absolutely convergent for every $x$, the function $T_hu$ is smooth, and its real Fréchet derivative satisfies $$D(T_hu)(x)[v]=\int_{\mathbf R^m}Dh(x-y)[v]u(y)\,dy\qquad(x,v\in\mathbf R^m).$$
